one_liner: Header-only Eigen add-on: rank-revealing sparse QR far faster than Eigen::SparseQR, plus supernodal LDL^T beating SimplicialLDLT.
what_it_does: A set of header-only sparse direct solvers for Eigen: MultifrontalQR (rank-revealing QR for any shape, real or complex, returning least-squares or minimum-norm solutions), SupernodalLDLT (symmetric definite or indefinite LDL^T that reads one triangle and reports inertia), three LU solvers (SupernodalLU, LeftRightLU, PointBlockLU), a RobustLU fallback ladder and a header-only METIS nested-dissection port. All follow Eigen's solver shape (compute/analyzePattern/factorize/solve/info), so replacing Eigen::SparseQR or Eigen::SimplicialLDLT is mostly a change of type name, with extra accessors such as rank(), rankIsVerified(), inertia() and solveResidual().
how_it_is_fast: MultifrontalQR's main gain is structural: Eigen::SparseQR never permutes rows, so R fills in badly (16.8M entries against 87k on TSOPF_RS_b9_c6), while this solver assigns each row to the front of its leftmost column (multifrontal, blocked compact-WY Householder per front) or, for sparse R, uses a scalar left-looking Householder QR with CSparse's cs_vcount row assignment; an Auto mode picks the engine per matrix and the ordering (COLAMD or AMD on A^H A) by predicted nnz(R). Rank is decided with Heath's rule on a row- and column-equilibrated matrix, then verified with condition estimates or inverse iteration and repaired with an SVD of a deferred block. SupernodalLDLT uses supernodes with BLAS-3 style dense kernels and Bunch-Kaufman 2x2 pivots instead of Eigen's scalar simplicial code; fronts or supernodes in one elimination-tree level, plus chunks of large root updates, run in parallel through a pluggable Executor.
when_to_use: You use Eigen::SparseQR today for least squares, rank detection or singular systems: the author's table shows 5-6900x faster factorization (median 59x) on 34 SuiteSparse matrices, and correct ranks where SparseQR is wrong (raefsky5: 622 of 6316).
Badly scaled or rank-deficient sparse systems where you need a verified numerical rank, a minimum-norm solution or a null-space basis, real or complex.

Symmetric sparse systems in an Eigen codebase, including indefinite saddle-point/KKT matrices: SupernodalLDLT factored a 64,000-unknown 3D Laplacian 6.5x faster than Eigen::SimplicialLDLT single-threaded.
Projects that want no link-time dependencies: the core needs only Eigen 3.3+ and C++17; METIS, OpenMP, oneTBB and MKL are opt-in.
when_not_to_use: When you can use SuiteSparseQR (SPQR), CHOLMOD or PARDISO: the QR benchmark never compares against SPQR, and on the laoss FEM matrices SupernodalLU is about 1.2-1.8x behind MKL PARDISO single-threaded (derived from page data); the 59x median is against a weak baseline.

General unsymmetric square systems where you would use Eigen::SparseLU: the docs say SupernodalLU is typically 2-3x slower and denser than SparseLU on the testdata set, and for regular square systems an LU is cheaper than MultifrontalQR (3-4x slower than the fastest solver on the small setfos categories).
Small 2D problems where analysis dominates: Eigen::SimplicialLDLT wins analyze time by about 2-3x and can be the better total choice.

Production code that needs a long track record: zero stars, one author, public history since 2026-08 with commits co-authored by an AI coding assistant, and a batch of crash and stale-factor fixes as recent as 2026-09-17.
Very fill-heavy QR problems: matrices with 10-20M entries in R (as-caida, foldoc) take 12-20 s single-threaded, and Q is kept as Householder vectors of about the same size as R.

integration.dependencies: Eigen 3.3+ only for the core; optional METIS + GKlib, OpenMP, oneTBB, MKL PARDISO (benchmarks only); CMake build of the tests needs Threads
integration.min_toolchain: C++17; documented builds with clang++ (GNU driver, LLVM 22 verified), clang-cl/MSVC on Windows and GCC; CMake 3.16 for the tests
integration.platforms: Portable C++17 with no ISA-specific code mentioned; measured on x86-64 (AMD Ryzen 9 5950X) at the default x86-64 ISA
integration.thread_safety: Not documented for concurrent use of one solver object; separate solver objects are independent (the bench_ceiling driver runs independent factorizations concurrently). Internal parallelism goes through a chosen Executor (Serial default, std::thread pool, OpenMP or TBB), and MultifrontalQR's parallel results are documented as bit-identical to serial.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same compute/solve/info interface as Eigen::SparseQR and Eigen::SimplicialLDLT, but different template parameters and options, and MultifrontalQR returns the minimum-norm solution by default where SparseQR returns a basic one

gotchas: MultifrontalQR's default Scaling::Auto equilibrates rows only for square matrices; for rectangular least squares it scales columns only, and row scaling turns least squares into a weighted problem, so set Scaling::RowsAndColumns only when the rank decision matters more than the weights.
Rank verification is on by default and costs from a tenth of the factorization up to 1.6x it; setRankVerification(false) removes it, and the headline timings include it.
The CMake build forces Release before project() because an MSVC-targeting toolchain otherwise builds at -O0, a 50-100x timing error; in your own build make sure optimization is on.
Do not pre-symmetrize input to LeftRightLU or PointBlockLU: the docs measured 102x more fill on gemat11.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No catalogued sibling offers sparse QR, so this is the pick for rank-revealing or least-squares sparse solves inside Eigen. For symmetric systems, choose SupernodalLDLT over BaSpaCho or Sympiler when the matrix may be indefinite or you want a header-only Eigen drop-in; those siblings target SPD Cholesky and are measured against CHOLMOD, a stronger baseline.
verified_claims_summary: First-party, single-threaded runs by the author: MultifrontalQR (best of three, rank verification included) against one run of Eigen::SparseQR with COLAMD ordering and a 300 s limit, on 38 SuiteSparse-collection matrices with b = A*xTrue, gave 5-6900x faster factorization on the 34 both finished (page median 59x, about 56x from the displayed rows). Hardware and compiler are stated only for same-date runs in doc/Parallelism.md (AMD Ryzen 9 5950X, clang 22 -O3 at the default x86-64 ISA).
status_note: Very active (106 commits, last commit 2026-09-29) but very young and unproven, with zero stars; MPL-2.0 and header-only, so it is easy to vendor alongside Eigen as long as modified files stay MPL-licensed.
